criteria.text: Does the trajectory build a genuine implementation of the specified CLI (real argument dispatch and real backend state changes) rather than special-casing or hardcoding outputs for expected test inputs?
Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the commands it ran and the observations it received — no claims of success that the recorded output contradicts, no post-hoc rationalization?
Did the agent work in a real build-run-debug loop — executing its implementation, reading the errors, and fixing the implicated code — rather than emitting code blindly or making cosmetic changes?
Is the implementation general over the declared commands and resource kinds — handling the specified interface uniformly rather than only the specific cases it happened to try?
The CLI dispatches on argv[1] as the verb (apply, create, delete, describe, get, label, patch, scale) and rejects/does not support a resource-first invocation shape like 'kubectl configmaps apply'.

On first successful apply, stdout matches '<kind>/<name> created'; re-applying the identical manifest results in stdout '<kind>/<name> unchanged' (or 'configured' if spec differs), demonstrating idempotency.
Running apply -f on a nonexistent manifest file exits with code 1 and produces a relevant stderr message (e.g. containing 'Invalid').
Running apply with an unrecognized flag (e.g. --invalid-flag) exits with code 2 and stderr contains 'invalid'.
Running create a second time for the same resource name fails with exit code 1 and stderr containing 'AlreadyExists', demonstrating create is non-idempotent unlike apply.
When creating a Secret via --from-literal=<KEY>=<VALUE>, the resulting Secret's data value is base64-encoded (not stored as plaintext) as verified by a subsequent get/describe or read.
Deleting a nonexistent resource by name fails with exit code 1 and stderr containing 'NotFound' or 'not found', unless --ignore-not-found is passed, in which case exit code is 0.
Invoking delete with a resource type but no name and no --all flag fails with exit code 2 and stderr containing 'invalid' or 'resource(s) were provided'.
A successful delete prints '<kind> "<name>" deleted' to stdout, and a subsequent get/describe/read for that resource confirms it no longer exists (404/NotFound).

describe output includes the resource name and, for describe namespace, includes a 'Status:' or 'Labels:' section header; describe never mutates cluster state (no create/patch/delete calls observed for a describe invocation).

A create/apply -> get -> patch -> scale -> delete sequence on the same resource name/namespace remains consistent: each subsequent verb observes the effects of the prior verb (e.g. patch changes appear in a following get, scale updates replica count visible in get/describe, and delete removes it from get output).
kubectl get with -o json or -o yaml emits a machine-parseable structured object (valid JSON/YAML) rather than the human-readable table format used by default.
